answer: Each identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle every epoch, with difficulty scaling per funding cluster: the first identity from one wallet pays 1 compute unit, the second 4, the third 16, compounding like ice off a glacier. An attacker finds no ledge: 100 linked fakes cost about 100 times honest compute, since cluster links come from on-chain funding. A sable identity stays cheap to keep while a sybil herd grows quadratically costly. Validators replay each proof and cluster factor, rejecting identities whose difficulty mismatches their cluster size.
